headline: AIIMS New Delhi launches AIR CARE study on air pollution and lung cancer
dek: News18 reports that AIIMS New Delhi has started a three-year population-level study of long-term air pollution exposure and lung cancer, including in never-smokers.
body:
AIIMS New Delhi has launched a study called AIR CARE to examine how long-term exposure to air pollution may contribute to lung cancer, according to a post on X by News18 on 14 November 2026.

News18 described AIR CARE as India's first population-level study of its kind. The post said the study will look at the possible role of long-term air pollution exposure in lung cancer, including among people who have never smoked.

According to the post, the study will run for three years and invites public participation. The post did not say how people can take part, how many participants will be recruited or what measurements will be used.

The post, which credited @shreyasharma_SS, asked whether the study could reshape what is known about air quality and health. That question was posed by News18 and is not a finding. No results have been reported, and the post covers only the launch of the study.
key_quote: The three-year study invites public participation.
